source_text: Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι: μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου: ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε.
thought_title: One Eucharist, one flesh, one altar
orientation: Ignatius is urging the Philadelphians to unite around the bishop and the single Eucharist, continuing his warning against division.
pass_a_gloss: Be eager therefore [with] one Eucharist to use: one for flesh of the Lord of us Jesus Christ and one cup for unity of the blood of him, one altar, as one bishop together with the council of elders and deacons the fellow-servants of me: so that, whatever you do, according to God you do.

choices.why: χράομαι with dative means to use or participate in; 'share in' captures the communal sense Ignatius intends

choices.english: for the unity of his blood
choices.why: εἰς with accusative expresses purpose; the cup brings about unity in Christ's blood
rejected: into the unity of his blood
toward the unity of his blood

choices.why: ὡς introduces a comparison; the single altar corresponds to the single bishop

choices.english: you may act according to God
choices.why: κατὰ with accusative means in accordance with; the purpose clause expresses that all action should align with God's will
rejected: you may do according to God
you may practice according to God

pass_b_english: Make every effort, then, to share in one Eucharist. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ and one cup that unites us in his blood, one altar, just as there is one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons, my fellow servants. Do this so that whatever you do, you may act according to God.

last_rejected.quote: for the unity of his blood
last_rejected.why: εἰς ἕνωσιν means 'into unity' or 'for unity,' but 'the unity of his blood' suggests the blood itself has unity, not that the cup leads to unity. The Greek means 'one cup unto/for unity of his blood'—the cup brings about unity through his blood.
last_rejected.fix: one cup that unites us in his blood, or one cup for our unity through his blood
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος naturally reads 'for the unity of his blood'; genitive αἵματος complements ἕνωσιν. Standard rendering, not misleading.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' is standard, but 'council of the apostles' and 'council of the bishop' appear once each; reader may miss these are the same institution.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note where source differs.

problems.why: Same Greek term (thysiastērion) rendered inconsistently with/without article; not serious but worth noting.
Same Greek term (syndoulos) rendered two ways; reader may not recognize these are identical.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'fellow servant' or note equivalence.

problems.quote: one cup for the unity of his blood
problems.why: 'Unity of his blood' is odd; means 'cup that unites us in his blood' or 'cup of his blood which creates unity.'
problems.fix: 'The cup that unites us in his blood.'

problems.why: The 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' are analogies for the elders, but may read as separate bodies.
problems.fix: Clarify these are analogies: 'council of elders—which corresponds to the council of the apostles.'

edits.old: one cup for the unity of his blood
edits.new: one cup that unites us in his blood

fixed: The 'council of elders' glossary note is consistent with the brief's glossary; no edit needed.
The 'altar' glossary note is consistent with the brief's glossary; no edit needed.
The 'fellow servant' glossary note is consistent with the brief's glossary; no edit needed.

The phrase 'one cup for the unity of his blood' misstates the source's 'εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ' (for unity of his blood); the cup is the means of unity in his blood, so I changed it to 'one cup that unites us in his blood.'
The 'council of elders' analogy note is consistent with the brief's glossary; no edit needed.
